Hi all — technical notes below. Landed on this after a quick runbook review and a short infra check: we can do tenant-scoped longer TTL for session logs with these constraints and controls.

1) Isolation model: we implement retention at the tenant-id level in our telemetry pipeline. Scoped retention means only objects tagged with your tenant ID are routed into the 180d tier. No org-wide TTL flip required.

2) Storage & encryption: longer TTL entries are stored in a tenant partition with server-side encryption using a tenant-specific KMS key (not shared with other tenants). We can provide KMS key IDs and rotation schedule snapshots as evidence (redacted key material).

3) Proof-of-delete: two accepted approaches (we can provide both):
   - Deletion manifest (JSON) with S3 object keys and deletion timestamps + signed hash (we sign manifests with a rotated service key and include the signature verification path).
   - Keystore revocation + zero-length tombstone with hash chain records (useful if objects are offloaded to archival buckets).

4) Sampling attestation: for audit, we can provide a sample proof-of-delete packet (redacted IDs) plus a SIG mapping that references applicable CAIQ items (logging retention, egress controls). See attached diagram and partial SIG response.

Constraints / caveats:
- Forensic hold: if you or any regulator issues a legal hold for specific objects, we will freeze deletion for the affected object set as an operational exception (we will notify your security lead).
- Cost / billing: 180d retention will be billed as additional storage on top of standard usage. We'll include an estimate in the exhibit.

I attached: redwood-segmentation-diagram.png, sig_response_partial.pdf, and a draft sample-manifest (we'll produce a clean sample that strips PII).

Happy to walk through this in a 30-minute tech call.

Ben Carter
